title: ConvergeStop: Inference-Time Convergence-Based Halting for Generative Text Embeddings

contributions.purpose: Cut the computational cost of generative text embeddings that use a fixed number of refinement iterations (e.g., GIRCSE's K=20).
contributions.mechanism: ConvergeStop, a training-free inference-time halting rule that tracks a running-mean embedding and halts when cosine similarity between consecutive intermediate embeddings exceeds a threshold tau for M consecutive steps.
contributions.evaluation: On SciFact, 55% compute reduction (average 9.10 vs 20 iterations) while matching full-refinement quality (78.33 vs 77.97 nDCG@10); on FiQA2018, +0.53 nDCG@10 over compute-matched baselines with 7% savings.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce ConvergeStop, an inference-time convergence-based halting rule for generative text embeddings that requires no additional training.

contributions.purpose: Validate the premise that embedding stability during generation is a usable halting signal.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical analysis of cosine-similarity stability of intermediate embeddings across refinement steps and its relation to retrieval ranking.
contributions.evaluation: Embedding stability increases monotonically with refinement steps and predicts retrieval-ranking stability.
contributions.source_quote: We empirically validate the convergence premise: embedding stability increases monotonically with refinement steps and predicts retrieval-ranking stability.

contributions.purpose: Show adaptive halting dominates fixed-iteration budgets on the quality-compute tradeoff.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of ConvergeStop against fixed-K baselines across compute budgets on two BEIR retrieval benchmarks (SciFact, FiQA2018).
contributions.evaluation: ConvergeStop operates above the Pareto frontier defined by fixed-K baselines, achieving better quality-compute tradeoffs through adaptive halting.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that ConvergeStop operates above the Pareto frontier defined by fixed-K baselines, achieving better quality-compute tradeoffs through adaptive halting.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work draws inspiration from these methods but operates at inference time without requiring additional training.
Unlike these methods that reduce embedding dimensions, ConvergeStop reduces the number of refinement iterations while preserving full embedding dimensionality.

ConvergeStop halts when the cosine similarity between consecutive embeddings exceeds a threshold tau for M consecutive steps, inspired by patience-based early exit methods in adaptive computation (Graves, 2016; Zhou et al., 2020).

notes: Paper itself flags dataset-dependent efficiency: large savings on SciFact (55%) but only modest 7% on FiQA2018; gains depend on how quickly embeddings converge per domain.
